title: Contrast, readability, and accessible colour use
learningObjectives: Explain contrast, readability, and accessible colour use and apply it correctly in a small CSS example.

understand.concept: Colour contrast is the difference in relative luminance between foreground and background. For ordinary text, WCAG 2.2 AA generally requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1; large text generally requires 3:1. Colour must not be the only way information is communicated.
understand.whyItMatters: A visually attractive palette can still make text difficult to read. Check text, controls, focus indicators, hover states, and disabled states. Ratios are calculated from relative luminance, not by comparing RGB channel values directly.
understand.analogy: Think of reading dark writing on a pale page versus pale writing on a similar pale page. The amount of visual separation matters more than whether the colours are fashionable.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps build intuition, but the browser follows the CSS specifications and computed-style rules rather than human intentions.

explain.narrative: The first sample is deliberately high contrast; the second is deliberately difficult to read. Do not rely on the coloured dot alone to communicate meaning.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to learn the effect of a CSS value?
options: Change one value and inspect the rendered result
Add unrelated declarations until it looks right
Assume every browser calculates styles identically in every context
